Short Reads

Just the decision, for busy days.
Every interview, in three lines.

  1. ST.005Sep 28, 2026Mariko Hayase

    Her father ran the line for 40 years. As his successor, she shut it down

    1. Orders for their core auto parts fell by half in three years.
    2. She shut the mass-production line and focused on prototype machining.
    3. No craftsman left, and revenue recovered within two years.

    Read the story→8 min

  2. ST.004Sep 22, 2026Takuma Nakamura

    He started the company with his best friend from college. Then he asked him to leave

    1. With equal shares and equal authority, nobody had the final say.
    2. After six months of talks, he asked his co-founder to step down.
    3. They still go out for a drink together once a year.

    Read the story→7 min

  3. ST.003Sep 8, 2026Keisuke Mori

    He left to protect it: 143 days to walk away from the company he founded

    1. Every decision ran through the founder, and the organization slowed down.
    2. Before choosing a successor, he gave up his own role.
    3. Over 143 days he handed over authority and stepped outside.

    Read the story→7 min

  4. ST.002Sep 10, 2026Nao Kuroda

    She knew it would fail. It still took her a year to stop

    1. Revenue was growing, but few customers stayed past three months.
    2. Encouraging messages led her to move the exit line three times.
    3. She made the rule impossible to change alone — and closed the business.

    Read the story→6 min

  5. ST.001Sep 12, 2026Ryo Saeki

    The morning after he decided to close the company, he couldn’t say a word

    1. Two months of cash left, and the CEO had decided to close.
    2. Faced with a rescue plan his team wrote overnight, he held back the announcement.
    3. He chose to keep the customers, not the size of the company.

    Read the story→8 min
